turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
I'll investigate the repo structure using the GitHub API via `gh` without cloning.Good, this gives a clear picture. Let me look at the core streaming implementation and how the API methods (chat completions, responses) wire into it.This confirms the core mechanism. Now let's check how the public `create()` methods in chat/completions.ts and responses.ts set `stream: true` and route into this.I have enough evidence now. Let me quickly confirm the `AssistantStream` and `ResponseStream` (lib/responses) tie back to core `Stream` as well, then write up findings.## Streaming implementation in openai-node

**Core transport layer** — `src/core/streaming.ts` (re-exported for back-compat by the deprecated `src/streaming.ts`)
- `class Stream<Item>` — wraps an `AsyncIterable`, exposes `.tee()` and `.toReadableStream()`.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse(response, controller, client, synthesizeEventData)` — parses a `Response` body as Server-Sent Events (via the internal `_iterSSEMessages`/`SSEDecoder`/`iterSSEChunks` helpers in the same file) into JSON-parsed items, raising `APIError` on `data.error` and stopping at `data: [DONE]`.
- `Stream.fromReadableStream(readableStream, controller, client)` — parses a newline-delimited JSON `ReadableStream` (used for things like Assistants raw streams).

**Dispatch point** — `src/internal/parse.ts`, function `defaultParseResponse`
- Checks `props.options.stream`; if true, calls `props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(...)` (or `Stream.fromSSEResponse` as the default) instead of parsing JSON/text. This is the single choke point where every streaming request becomes a `Stream<Item>` — confirmed by reading the file directly.

**Higher-level, ergonomic stream wrappers** (all built on top of `core/streaming.ts`, via `src/lib/EventStream.ts`'s `EventStream<EventTypes>` base class which adds `on()`/`.done()`/promise-style ergonomics):
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` — `ChatCompletionStream` (extends `AbstractChatCompletionRunner` → `EventStream`); `static createChatCompletion(...)` and `static fromReadableStream(...)` call `Stream.fromSSEResponse`/`Stream.fromReadableStream` internally.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` — tool-calling runner variant used when `.runTools()` is called with `stream: true`.
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` — `ResponseStream` (extends `EventStream`), `static createResponse(...)`.
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` — `AssistantStream` (extends `EventStream`), `static createToolAssistantStream(...)` / `static fromReadableStream(...)` for the (legacy) Assistants API runs.

## Public API methods that route into streaming

Verified by reading each resource file directly:

1. **`client.chat.completions.create(body, options)`** — `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:61-79`. Overloaded on `ChatCompletionCreateParamsStreaming` (`stream: true`) vs `...NonStreaming`. Implementation calls `this._client.post('/chat/completions', { body, stream: body.stream ?? false, ... })`, so when `stream: true` the returned `APIPromise` resolves to `Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>` via `defaultParseResponse`.
2. **`client.chat.completions.stream(body, options)`** — same file, line ~221-225: `return ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion(this._client, body, options)`.
3. **`client.chat.completions.runTools(body, options)`** — line ~206-211: if `body.stream`, delegates to `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.runTools(...)`.
4. **`client.responses.create(body, options)`** — `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:96-122`. Same pattern: `this._client.post('/responses', { body, stream: body.stream ?? false, ... })`, overloaded for `ResponseCreateParamsStreaming` → `APIPromise<Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>>`.
5. **`client.responses.retrieve(id, query, options)`** — same file, ~137-168: also overloaded on `query.stream`, passing `stream: query?.stream ?? false` to `this._client.get(...)`, so retrieving a background/in-flight response can also come back as a `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>`.
6. **`client.responses.stream(body, options)`** — line ~201-205: `return ResponseStream.createResponse<ParsedT>(this._client, body, options)`.
7. Legacy **Assistants** run-streaming methods build on `AssistantStream` (`src/lib/AssistantStream.ts`), e.g. `runs.stream()` / `runs.createAndStream()` (not re-verified line-by-line, see caveat below), which use `AssistantStream.fromReadableStream`/SSE parsing under `event.startsWith('thread.')` handling visible in `core/streaming.ts`'s `Stream.fromSSEResponse`.

Other endpoints reuse the identical `stream: body.stream ?? false` pattern for streaming variants (grep hits in `client.ts` show `CompletionCreateParamsStreaming` for legacy completions and `ImageEditParamsStreaming`/`ImageGenerateParamsStreaming` for partial-image streaming), all funneling through the same `defaultParseResponse` → `Stream.fromSSEResponse` path.

**Not verified / out of scope of this pass:**
- I did not open `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts` (or equivalent) to confirm the exact `runs.stream()`/`runs.createAndStream()` signatures — I'm inferring their existence from `AssistantStream`'s exported factory methods and the `thread.*` event branch in `Stream.fromSSEResponse`, not from reading the runs resource file directly.
- I did not check `src/resources/completions.ts` (legacy Completions API) or the images resource file line-by-line for their streaming overloads — only confirmed via grep hits in `client.ts` that `CompletionCreateParamsStreaming`/`ImageEditParamsStreaming`/`ImageGenerateParamsStreaming` exist.
- I did not run the code or test suite; all conclusions are from static reading of source via the GitHub API (`gh api .../contents/...`) against the `main` branch as of now (2026-07-06).
